item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00032","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C14","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 is a clear, concrete drafting template for the child. Both orders use nearly identical recitals describing a labor dispute that threatens a strike or lockout in interstate commerce and imperils national safety, followed by the same Title II board machinery, a section 206 reporting deadline, and continued board existence until presidential termination. The child principally substitutes the disputants, industry, factual details, deadline, and adds national health. C14 and C18 are weaker parallels involving labor-dispute boards and presidential reports, but they proceed under the Railway Labor Act and use materially different procedures.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between Swift and Company...and certain of their employees...involving wages","parent_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between the Carbide and Carbon Chemicals Corporation and certain of its employees...involving wages and terms and conditions of employment","explanation":"The opening recital follows the same dispute-party-subject formulation, adapted to different employers and employees."},{"child_excerpt":"such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of the meat-packing industry, an industry engaged in trade or commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in the production of goods for commerce, which strike or lock-out, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national health and safety","parent_excerpt":"such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in the production of goods for commerce, which strike or lock-out, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national safety","explanation":"This is highly distinctive, nearly verbatim language; the child specifies the meat-packing industry and adds health to the threatened national interests."},{"child_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before April 1, 1948.","parent_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before March 19, 1948.","explanation":"The operative authority and reporting mechanism are essentially identical, with only the deadline changed."},{"child_excerpt":"Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","parent_excerpt":"Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","explanation":"The concluding operative provision is verbatim, confirming both literal reuse and the same administrative structure."}]}
